newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel likely to raise 1996 investment budget.
newsitem.headline: Israel likely to raise 1996 investment budget.

text.p: Israel's Finance Ministry will probably increase the Investment Centre's 1996 budget by 300 million shekels ($94 million), a Treasury spokesman said.

The centre, the Industry and Trade Ministry's arm responsible for capital investment subsidies, had requested an additional 300 million shekels because it has used up its funds and cannot approve any more projects this year. The centre's 1996 budget was originally 1.8 billion shekels.
"The Investment Centre has no more budget to approve investments this year," a spokeswoman for the centre said.

Israel's government plans to cut investment subsidies in 1997. Under the proposal, which still needs parliamentary approval, the maximum grant in top priority areas would be reduced to 20 percent from 34 percent.

Projects that are approved by the centre this year will be eligible for a smaller subsidy next year. Vishay Intertechnology has already said that if it does not get a 34 percent subsidy, it may not go ahead with plans for a $50 million plant in the development town of Ofakim. ($1 = 3.19 shekels)
